questions.q: Determine dry weight from wet weight and water loss. Use the method 'Chemical Analysis of Living Tissues'. Work with: filtrate_mass = 8, retentate_mass = 10, water_mass = 50, wet_weight = 240. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of acid_insoluble_fraction.

Calculate the dry weight of a plant tissue sample. Use the method 'Chemical Analysis of Living Tissues'. Work with: filtrate_mass = 12, retentate_mass = 40, water_mass = 12, wet_weight = 500. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of acid_insoluble_fraction.
Explain in your own words what 'Chemical Analysis of Living Tissues' refers to.
questions.a: Chemical extraction using trichloroacetic acid separates cellular contents into an acid-soluble filtrate of low molecular weight compounds and an acid-insoluble retentate.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Chemical Analysis of Living Tissues'.
questions.a: Acid fractionation separates low molecular weight metabolites from macromolecular insoluble cellular structures.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Chemical Analysis of Living Tissues', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate total metabolite types from primary and secondary counts. Use the method 'Primary and Secondary Metabolites'. Work with: primary_count = 50, secondary_count = 8. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_metabolites.

Find total number of identified metabolic compounds. Use the method 'Primary and Secondary Metabolites'. Work with: primary_count = 30, secondary_count = 4. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_metabolites.
Explain in your own words what 'Primary and Secondary Metabolites' refers to.
questions.a: Cellular organic molecules are grouped into primary metabolites essential for fundamental physiology and secondary metabolites serving specialized ecological roles.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Primary and Secondary Metabolites'.
questions.a: Primary metabolites participate in basic living processes while secondary metabolites provide defense, coloration, or industrial utility.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Primary and Secondary Metabolites', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate the mass of cellular protein from percentage in Class 11 biology. Use the method 'Cellular Mass and Biomacromolecules Composition'. Work with: percentage = 25, total_cell_mass = 500. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of component_mass.

Find the weight of water in cell given total cell mass. Use the method 'Cellular Mass and Biomacromolecules Composition'. Work with: percentage = 12, total_cell_mass = 10. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of component_mass.
Explain in your own words what 'Cellular Mass and Biomacromolecules Composition' refers to.
questions.a: Quantitative distribution of cellular components where macromolecules like proteins form the insoluble fraction while water dominates overall mass.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Cellular Mass and Biomacromolecules Composition'.
questions.a: Biomacromolecules feature molecular weights above ten thousand daltons and make up most cellular structural dry weight.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Cellular Mass and Biomacromolecules Composition', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate number of peptide bonds in a linear protein chain. Use the method 'Proteins and Amino Acid Linkages'. Work with: amino_acid_count = 500. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of peptide_bonds.

Find peptide bond count for a given number of amino acids. Use the method 'Proteins and Amino Acid Linkages'. Work with: amino_acid_count = 10. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of peptide_bonds.
Explain in your own words what 'Proteins and Amino Acid Linkages' refers to.
questions.a: Proteins are heteropolymers composed of amino acid monomers linked together sequentially by covalent peptide bonds.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Proteins and Amino Acid Linkages'.
questions.a: Unbranched polypeptide chains of N amino acid units contain N minus one peptide bonds.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Proteins and Amino Acid Linkages', in plain ASCII form.

Find average monomer mass in a polysaccharide chain. Use the method 'Polysaccharides and Glycosidic Polymers'. Work with: monomer_count = 360, total_polymer_mass = 3. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of monosaccharide_mass.

Calculate average mass of monosaccharide unit in polysaccharide. Use the method 'Polysaccharides and Glycosidic Polymers'. Work with: monomer_count = 12, total_polymer_mass = 100. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of monosaccharide_mass.
Explain in your own words what 'Polysaccharides and Glycosidic Polymers' refers to.
questions.a: Long sugar chains joined by glycosidic bonds function as structural walls or stored energy reserves like starch and glycogen.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Polysaccharides and Glycosidic Polymers'.
questions.a: Complex polysaccharide chains consist of monosaccharide residues with distinct reducing and non-reducing ends.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Polysaccharides and Glycosidic Polymers', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate total nucleotides from purine and pyrimidine counts. Use the method 'Nucleic Acids and Nucleotide Structure'. Work with: purine_count = 3, pyrimidine_count = 500. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_nucleotides.

Find nucleotide count given purines and pyrimidines. Use the method 'Nucleic Acids and Nucleotide Structure'. Work with: purine_count = 150, pyrimidine_count = 12. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_nucleotides.
Explain in your own words what 'Nucleic Acids and Nucleotide Structure' refers to.
questions.a: Polynucleotides composed of nitrogenous bases, pentose sugars, and phosphate groups that store and transmit biological genetic information.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Nucleic Acids and Nucleotide Structure'.
questions.a: Nucleic acid polymers consist of purine and pyrimidine nucleotide monomers linked sequentially.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Nucleic Acids and Nucleotide Structure', in plain ASCII form.
Explain in your own words what 'Structural Organization of Proteins' refers to.
questions.a: Proteins organize into primary sequences, secondary helices or sheets, tertiary globular folds, and quaternary multi-subunit assemblies.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Structural Organization of Proteins'.
questions.a: Three-dimensional tertiary folding creates active sites required for catalytic and metabolic functions.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Structural Organization of Proteins' taught, and from which source text?

Calculate enzymatic reaction rate in Class 11 biology. Use the method 'Enzyme Catalysis and Reaction Rate'. Work with: catalysed_rate = 10, delta_p = 120, delta_t = 12, uncatalysed_rate = 5. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of rate_ratio.

Find rate of product formation per unit time. Use the method 'Enzyme Catalysis and Reaction Rate'. Work with: catalysed_rate = 15, delta_p = 50, delta_t = 6, uncatalysed_rate = 8. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of rate_ratio.
Explain in your own words what 'Enzyme Catalysis and Reaction Rate' refers to.
questions.a: Enzymatic reaction rate represents the quantity of substrate converted into product per unit time.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Enzyme Catalysis and Reaction Rate'.
questions.a: Enzymes greatly accelerate chemical conversion rates compared to uncatalysed background reactions.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Enzyme Catalysis and Reaction Rate', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate fold acceleration of reaction by enzyme. Use the method 'Activation Energy and Catalytic Acceleration'. Work with: catalysed_rate = 5, uncatalysed_rate = 8. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of fold_acceleration.

Find rate increase factor comparing catalysed and uncatalysed reaction. Use the method 'Activation Energy and Catalytic Acceleration'. Work with: catalysed_rate = 5, uncatalysed_rate = 15. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of fold_acceleration.
Explain in your own words what 'Activation Energy and Catalytic Acceleration' refers to.
questions.a: Enzymes lower the activation energy barrier necessary to reach the high-energy transition state, increasing conversion speed.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Activation Energy and Catalytic Acceleration'.
questions.a: Substrate binding at active sites lowers activation energy to accelerate chemical transformation.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Activation Energy and Catalytic Acceleration', in plain ASCII form.

concepts.title: Enzyme Kinetics and Factors Affecting Activity

questions.q: Calculate half maximum velocity from Vmax in Class 11 biology. Use the method 'Enzyme Kinetics and Factors Affecting Activity'. Work with: vmax = 5. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of half_vmax.

Find half Vmax value for enzyme kinetics curve. Use the method 'Enzyme Kinetics and Factors Affecting Activity'. Work with: vmax = 3. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of half_vmax.
Explain in your own words what 'Enzyme Kinetics and Factors Affecting Activity' refers to.
questions.a: Enzyme velocity increases with substrate concentration until reaching maximum velocity Vmax, influenced by pH, temperature, and inhibitors.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Enzyme Kinetics and Factors Affecting Activity'.
questions.a: Saturation of active sites at high substrate concentration defines maximum enzymatic rate Vmax.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Enzyme Kinetics and Factors Affecting Activity', in plain ASCII form.
Explain in your own words what 'Enzyme Classification and Co-factors' refers to.
questions.a: Enzymes are classified into six categories based on reaction type, requiring non-protein cofactors for full catalytic function.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Enzyme Classification and Co-factors'.
questions.a: Active holoenzyme consists of the protein apoenzyme combined with organic or inorganic cofactors.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Enzyme Classification and Co-factors' taught, and from which source text?
